residual_risks: The 171-case suite uses synthetic stream-json and process fixtures; live Claude Code formal execution remains UNVERIFIED_RUNTIME.
Endpoint equality does not establish temporal immutability, so an otherwise PASS-TRACKED result remains capped at PASS-SCOPED.
The runtime identity binds the resolved entrypoint bytes, not the transitive interpreter, shared-library, kernel, or host dependency closure.
claims.text: The formal runner authenticates a would-be PASS-TRACKED run only when the certificate gate passes and a bounded complete runtime stream authenticates the exact native ntt-* call and result lanes with valid roles, unique matching IDs, and call-before-result ordering. Execution requires supported Linux child-subreaper plus process-group containment before Popen and fails closed on unavailable containment, malformed, duplicated, reordered, or oversized traces, or surviving same-group, detached-session, deep-chain, timeout, overflow, or inherited-pipe descendants. Results bind endpoint-checked target and runtime identities plus the exact prompt, complete transcript, and gate/certificate companions. Formal output checks are recomputed from nonempty report and gate content rather than self-attested, and results are written through directory capabilities acquired component-by-component without following links and held across evaluation. Canonical-result versus compatibility-JSON classification is frozen before execution. Live transcript/JSON outputs and the deterministic wrapper JSON outputs likewise acquire their parents before long work, reject cross-output aliases, and cannot be redirected by ancestor substitution. Children receive only runner-owned /proc/<runner-pid>/fd/N, authenticated by procfs-visible Pid and direct-parent PPid so child-FD close/rebind cannot substitute the capability; unsupported procfd inheritance fails before requested output mutation. These endpoint/capability observations are not temporal isolation. Results remain capped at PASS-SCOPED because temporal immutability is not mechanically enforced.
